rounds.text: Shankar Lal Rampal Dye-Chem Ltd demonstrates outstanding top-line expansion, boasting a compounded sales growth rate of 33% over 10 years and 21% over 5 years [E14, E15]. This robust commercial performance is reinforced by strong recent momentum, with trailing twelve-month sales growing 16% and net profit jumping 90% year-on-year [E17, E64]. Fundamental efficiency metrics further validate the underlying business strength, showing an above-sector return on assets of 8.62% versus the 6.13% benchmark and a healthy ROCE of 13.04% [E8, E10]. Valuation remains highly attractive relative to intrinsic worth, as a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 53 per share against a market price of Rs 37.9, providing a solid margin of safety of 28.4% [E43, E44]. Furthermore, the company operates with a conservatively financed balance sheet, evidenced by a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.20x as of March 2026 [E37]. Conceded: the stock currently suffers from weak price momentum, trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative-strength rating of zero [E48, E49].

Shankar Lal Rampal Dye-Chem Ltd is fundamentally under-appreciated, trading at an attractive P/E of 18.1x compared to the sector benchmark of 22.59x [E1, E6]. The business demonstrates robust long-term expansion, boasting a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of 33% and a 10-year compounded profit growth rate of 63% [E14, E18]. Recent performance also shows strong momentum, with trailing twelve-month sales growth at 16% and profit growth at 18%, alongside a notable turnaround reflected in a 100/100 results score with net profit up 90% year-on-year [E17, E21, E69]. Furthermore, the company's return on assets of 8.62% outpaces the sector benchmark of 6.13%, and its debt-to-equity ratio of 0.20x confirms it is conservatively financed [E8, E37]. A discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 53 per share against a market price of Rs 37.9, providing a clear margin of safety of 28.4% [E43, E44]. Conceded: the stock sits near its 52-week low with a 1-year price return of -52.7% and negative operating cash flows of Rs -7 Cr in Mar 2026 [E5, E34, E50].
